source.title: Resolving new memories: a critical look at the dentate gyrus, adult neurogenesis, and pattern separation

confidence_rationale: Canonical review proposing the 'memory resolution' hypothesis: broadly-tuned immature young neurons contribute different information than highly specific mature neurons. This is the cleanest literature analogue of Q-057's single-cue (broad/immature) vs convergent-weak-input (specific/mature) recall distinction, and it frames maturation as a change in recall specificity. Confidence moderate: it is a conceptual/theoretical review (2011), the maturation axis is at the cell level (young vs mature neurons), not whole-system development, and the mapping to REE cue-authority is interpretive.
failure_signatures: The paper notes a persistent reconciliation problem -- the 'pattern separation' tested behaviourally does not match the computational/electrophysiological conception -- so importing 'pattern separation/completion' vocabulary into REE without operational care risks the same equivocation.
Resolution is framed as a continuum of neuronal tuning width, not a discrete developmental gate; an REE account that posits a sharp gate before action-release may over-discretise a graded property.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Under the 'memory resolution' hypothesis, broadly-tuned immature adult-born granule cells and highly specific mature granule cells make distinct information contributions; the fidelity (resolution) of a memory, and its spatial/contextual discriminability, depends on the balance of these contributions rather than on pattern separation alone.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports Q-057's first sub-question by giving a mechanistic precedent for recall regimes that change with maturation: a broad, low-specificity (immature) regime versus a narrow, high-specificity (mature) regime. This is the biological shape of 'immature single-cue authority vs mature convergent-weak-input recall' and constrains how REE should think about MECH-362/ARC-019 cue specificity maturing over development.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The maturation axis in this paper is the immature-vs-mature status of individual adult-born neurons, not organismal development of CA3 cue-authority. The hypothesis is theoretical and predates much of the causal optogenetic work; mapping 'tuning-width continuum' to REE's cue-authority gate is an analogy and risks the very pattern-separation equivocation the paper warns about.
mapping.source_context: Theoretical/critical review of dentate gyrus, adult hippocampal neurogenesis, and pattern separation; rodent + computational framing.

confidence_components.notes: Canonical Neuron review, well cited; but theoretical and cell-level rather than developmental-systems-level, so mapping fidelity and transfer risk are both moderate.
